Global Renewable Energy Adoption Reaches New Record in 2025

By Dr. Sarah Jenkins, Senior Energy Policy Analyst | Published November 14, 2025

Global installations of solar photovoltaic systems and utility-scale offshore wind farms expanded by 24% over the prior fiscal year, according to newly published datasets from the International Energy Agency (IEA).

Researchers analyzed grid interconnect queues across North America, the European Union, and East Asia. "The acceleration is primarily driven by plummeting battery storage costs and standardized municipal permitting," said lead analyst Marcus Vance at the Stockholm Energy Institute during an on-the-record interview.

The annual report highlights that solar generation capacity surpassed 580 gigawatts worldwide, with distributed commercial rooftop installations leading overall growth in mid-sized metropolitan areas.

However, independent transmission engineers caution that significant infrastructure challenges remain. Transmission line congestion, grid modernization backlogs, and rare earth mineral supply chains could constrain expansion if high-voltage direct current (HVDC) corridors are not prioritized by regional grid operators.

A spokesperson for the North American Grid Reliability Corporation confirmed that while localized curtailments occurred during peak summer generation, overall grid stability metrics met all statutory reliability thresholds throughout the operating season.
